public_rationale: The post, published 2024-12-03, forecasts with no deadline that big tech's scaling spending will produce neither AGI nor a product that justifies its cost. The contract lets this be settled early only by a widely recognized AGI demonstration, by filings showing AI profits cover cumulative AI capex, or by the named firms abandoning or impairing their AI build-outs for lack of returns. The one evidence item is background. In The Register on 2024-11-01, an Informa analyst estimated that hyperscalers had spent about $200 billion in capex since the start of 2023, while AI services brought in only about $20 billion in revenue. That figure comes from before the post and describes where the forecast started, not how it turned out. The packet contains no evidence that meets either early-resolution rule. The forecast remains open.
limitations: The packet holds one context item, dated before the post. It does not show whether any qualifying AGI demonstration, payback disclosure, or abandonment or impairment has happened since.
The $200 billion and $20 billion figures are one analyst's estimates across hyperscalers. They are not company disclosures and are not broken out for each named firm.
'Justify the costs' has no stated threshold or payback period, and AGI has no agreed definition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Big tech's strategy of scaling data centers, GPUs and training data will not produce AGI or a product that justifies the costs.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Google have all burned billions on the assumption that doing so would create something — be it a human-level "artificial general intelligence" or, I dunno, a product that would justify the costs — and it's become painfully obvious that it isn't going to work.

from_speaker: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Google have all burned billions
on the assumption that doing so would create something
or a product that would justify the costs
our_interpretation: This is a forecast with no deadline: big tech's scaling strategy will produce neither AGI nor a product whose returns justify the spending.
'Justify the costs' is read plainly: AI revenue and profit large enough to earn back the AI capital spending.
'Isn't going to work' cannot be shown true before some end point, so it can only be settled early by a decisive event.
criteria.support_condition: The named companies publicly abandon or sharply write down their AI build-outs, with impairments or capex cuts they attribute to failed AI returns, without having produced AGI or a product that pays for the spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A widely accepted demonstration of human-level AGI by one of these companies, or company disclosures showing that AI products earn returns that cover the scaling investment.
